name: decision theoretic explanation evaluation benchmark
description: Explanations of model behavior are commonly evaluated via proxy properties weakly tied to the purposes explanations serve in practice. We contribute a decision theoretic framework that treats explanations as information signals valued by the expected improvement they enable on a specified decision task. This approach yields three distinct estimands: 1) a theoretical benchmark that upperbounds achievable performance by any agent with the explanation, 2) a human-complementary value that quantifies the theoretically attainable value that is not already captured by a baseline human decision policy, and 3) a behavioral value representing the causal effect of providing the explanation to human decision-makers. We instantiate these definitions in a practical validation workflow, and apply them to assess explanation potential and interpret behavioral effects in human-AI decision support and mechanistic interpretability.
evaluation_method: expected utility / decision value estimation with human evaluation and causal effect analysis
reputation: A recent methodological benchmark/framework for evaluating explanations by their decision-theoretic value rather than proxy fidelity metrics.
notes: Not a conventional static benchmark; evaluation depends on the downstream decision task, human participants, and the chosen baseline policy.
